Subject: Dedicated capacity scenario and next steps (memory / context / precision)

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, Helix plans to run two heavy in-prod models: a 70B dense LLM (primary chat + long-context retrieval) and a 13B variant for high-concurrency inference on shorter contexts. Two asks to unblock sizing: a) a short worked example of how context length and KV cache requirements map to GPU memory across precision modes, and b) an initial reserved-pool footprint estimate we can use for procurement.

Quick constraints from your side: target tail latency 300–400ms for chat (99th), steady-state peak concurrent requests ~28, average prompt + response length ~1,200 tokens, and ~20% of calls will hit long-context retrieval flows with 64k windows.

I attached a CSV with the KV access profiling you shared and sketched two scenarios in the attached playbook. I’ll loop Marcus and Mina on the technical sizing notes below — Marcus for runtime/ops, Mina for model-footprint assumptions.

Proposed approach (short):
- Build per-model memory breakdown: model params (storage for quantized weights), optimizer/none for inference, KV cache for expected active context, and minimal host-side staging for offload.
- Evaluate two precision profiles: 4-bit (Q4/DQ) and 3-bit (Q3F) with mixed-int fallback for warm prefixes.
- Produce required GPU types and pool counts for two reserved tiers: baseline (no burst) and 20% headroom for spikes.

I’ll share a worked example in my next note. Please confirm if the concurrency and latency targets above are stable.

Thanks,
Jordan

Jordan / Mina —

I mocked up the worked example below using the Helix profile. Assumptions listed first so we can revise quickly:

Assumptions
- Primary model: 70B dense (fp16 baseline). Effective param storage by precision: FP16 ~ 140GB, Q4 ~ 35GB, Q3F ~ 26GB (includes packing overhead + per-layer alignment).
- KV cache cost: ~2 * model.hidden_size * context_tokens * token_embedding_bytes. For 70B, that maps to roughly 0.9–1.1 bytes per key-value pair when packed; practically ~0.9GB per 1k tokens in Q4 KV packing, ~0.7GB per 1k tokens in Q3F packing due to denser packing and per-kv compression.
- For a 64k window sustained active keys (worst-case long-context flow), estimated KV = 64 * (0.9GB per 1k) = ~57.6GB (Q4) or ~44.8GB (Q3F).
- Model execution scratch (activations, logits): plan for 12–24GB depending on batch/concurrency; we use conservative 20GB for 99th percentile.

Worked example (70B, 64k active KV):
- Q4 profile: quantized params 35GB + KV 58GB + exec scratch 20GB = ~113GB total GPU-resident memory.
- Q3F profile: params 26GB + KV 45GB + exec scratch 20GB = ~91GB total.

Operational interpretation:
- A single 80GB GPU cannot hold the full Q4 working set for the extreme 64k case; Q3F fits slightly above 80GB but still needs ~11GB host/peer staging. That implies either (a) use 2x80GB GPUs with NVLink (split KV/params and cross-device KV access), (b) move to 2x H100 80GB with NVLink + aggregate memory, or (c) accept KV offload to host (CPU) with small perf penalty.

For the 13B variant (short contexts, 2k typical):
- Q4 params ~6.5GB, KV for 2k ~1.8GB, exec scratch 6GB => fits comfortably on a single 32–40GB GPU in Q4. Q3F reduces params to ~5GB and KV to ~1.4GB.

I can translate these into pool counts given your concurrency numbers — see my ballpark below.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Capacity Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jordan / Marcus / Sam —

Adding ops notes and a conservative fleet layout for procurement:

Operational levers to reduce GPU headroom need:
- Active KV compression at production time (lossless packing we use in runtime reduces KV size by ~10–15% beyond raw Q packing).
- Prefix caching (store warm prefixes in per-GPU LRU) to avoid full-window KV for many calls — effective if long-context flows are <30% of traffic.
- Model variants routing: route short-context queries to 13B pool, long-context to reserved 70B nodes.
- Quantization selection: start Q4 for rapid onboarding, move to Q3F for reserved pools once quality sig tests pass. Q3F saves ~15–20% GPU memory in our measurements but requires additional validation.

Procurement footprint (baseline and committed reserve)
- Baseline: support steady peak concurrent 28 requests (mix 80% short-context to 20% long-context). Map capacity using effective concurrency per GPU: 70B long-context handling ~2 simultaneous inferences per H100 80GB equivalent (NVLink preferred); 13B handles ~10-12 short-context RPS per A40/3080-class card depending on batch.
- Recommended committed pool: 8x H100-80GB (NVLink) + 12x A40-48GB (or equivalent) for the 13B fleet. This yields ~support for the mix with 20% headroom and reasonable failover.
- Burst/ability to scale: allow auto-burst to hosted capacity and cross-region fallback for big experiments.

I attached a short playbook with the mapping and example cost delta between Q4 and Q3F profiles.

Mina

2) For the Q3F move: what is the expected timeline to qualify the 70B quality delta? We have a small internal eval set of 400 prompts — what pass rate should we target before committing?

If you can send a short note for procurement with the SKUs and a recommended validation checklist, we can fast-track to our procurement team next week.
